newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-MORE RAIN DELAYS WIMBLEDON'S FOURTH DAY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MORE RAIN DELAYS WIMBLEDON'S FOURTH DAY.

text.p: Rain continued to disrupt the Wimbledon tennis championships on Thursday, delaying the start of the fourth day.
Organisers, worried about the backlog after only two matches were completed on Wednesday, had planned to start play an hour early on Thursday, at 1000 GMT.
But more rain forced another delay though organisers said they still hoped to start play on the showcourts at 1100 GMT as planned.
World number one Martina Hingis was due to open the day's Centre Court action in a second-round match against Olga Barabanshchikova.

Tournament referee Alan Mills has said that the tournament could one or two days of delays and still finish on time. In 1991 the middle Sunday, traditionally a rest day, saw play in an attempt to catch up after only 52 matches had been played by Friday night.
Thursday's weather forecast offered little comfort for Mills with rain predicted for most of the day.
